key_takeaways: A wedding travel advisor plans the guest room block, flights, transfers and honeymoon as one trip, and is the person you call when something changes.

At Wedded Wonderland Travel, eligible stays at partner properties may include breakfast, a hotel credit and upgrade priority, confirmed in writing before you book, and these perks do not carry across a group room block automatically.

The ACCC says Australian Consumer Law guarantees apply whether you book direct or through an agent, but agents are usually bound by the supplier's terms, so an advisor's value lies in reading and negotiating those terms.
According to ATIA, accreditation is voluntary and is not a solvency guarantee or a compensation scheme.

At Wedded Wonderland, a straightforward hotel booking usually carries no planning fee, and any fee for complex itineraries, flights or group work is agreed upfront; ask any advisor who holds your deposits and in what currency.

faq.q: What is the difference between a travel advisor and a travel agent?
faq.a: In everyday use, very little: both plan and book travel, and 'advisor' usually signals more of the planning and advice. Neither title is a licence since, according to Consumer Affairs Victoria, state travel agent licensing was phased out from mid-2014, so look for ATIA accreditation and read the written terms.

faq.q: Do we need a travel advisor if we already have a wedding planner?
faq.a: A planner shapes the celebration and its vendors; a travel advisor moves guests, rooms and flights. If many of your guests are flying in, ask your planner who will manage the room block, transfers and the honeymoon, and get the answer in writing.

faq.q: Does using a travel advisor cost more than booking direct?
faq.a: It depends on how the advisor is paid on your booking, so ask before any work starts. At Wedded Wonderland, a straightforward hotel booking usually carries no planning fee, and more complex itineraries, flights or group work may carry a fee agreed upfront.

faq.q: Do our guests have to book inside the room block?
faq.a: That is their choice, but bookings made outside the block usually do not count toward it, so check how your contract counts pickup. If too few guests book inside, an attrition clause can charge the group, and unbooked rooms go back on sale after the cut-off date. Check both clauses before you sign and set the cut-off with your RSVP date in mind.

faq.q: Can a travel advisor plan our honeymoon as well as the wedding travel?
faq.a: Yes. We can stage the wedding at one resort and the honeymoon at another, or extend the same stay, with one specialist coordinating the whole trip.

faq.q: What happens if a guest's flight is cancelled before the wedding?
faq.a: The guest, or their advisor, contacts the airline first. Under Australian Consumer Law, if a service covered by the guarantees is not provided within a reasonable time, the provider must offer a replacement or refund; travel insurance with cancellation cover fills the gaps. This covers travel services within Australia and services by international businesses departing Australia; a guest flying in from overseas should check the airline's own terms and their travel insurance.
